Which covariates a checkpoint can condition on

Source: R/safetensors.R
timestral_supports_covariates.Rd

timestral_supports_covariates() is TRUE when the checkpoint was trained with covariates, so timestral_forecast() accepts past_covariates and categorical_past_covariates. timestral_supports_known_covariates() is TRUE when it can also condition on known-future covariates (known_covariates and categorical_known_covariates), which needs a block schedule that attends across variates. Both mirror the Python forecaster's supports_covariates and supports_known_covariates properties; every official checkpoint supports both.

Usage

timestral_supports_covariates(model)

timestral_supports_known_covariates(model)

Arguments

model

a timestral_model from timestral_load()

Value

TRUE or FALSE.

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
timestral_supports_covariates(m)
#> [1] TRUE
timestral_supports_known_covariates(m)
#> [1] TRUE
